text: In the Aditya Hrudayam, Lord Surya is called “Saptasapti”.
That means — the one who has seven horses.
But a question naturally arises, doesn't it,
Why seven?
It could be six… it could be eight… then why exactly seven?
Our scriptures themselves offer a beautiful insight into this.
The Rigveda describes that seven horses pull the Sun's chariot.
Yet in another place, it says—
“A single horse… with seven names.”
Which means…
Even if they appear as seven forms on the outside,
the power behind them is only one.
Later, the Srimad Bhagavatam gives an even clearer meaning to these seven horses.
They are described as symbols of the seven Chandas (poetic meters) of the Vedas—
Gayatri, Brihati, Ushnik, Jagati, Trishtup, Anushtup, Pankti.
Chandas means…
The rhythm and meter of a mantra.
Our tradition views such Sun God as the very source of knowledge — as the Guru to Hanuman, and as the deity revered by Sri Rama through Aditya Hrudayam before the battle with Ravana.
That is why the symbolic meaning here is so beautiful—
What carries a mantra forward is its Chandas.
What carries time forward is the Sun.
The single solar energy is intertwined with the rhythm of seven Chandas.
That is why He has this beautiful name — Saptasapti.
But this “seven” does not stop here.
We also see several other beautiful connections linked with the Sun and creation—
📅 Seven days — our weekly journey through the wheel of time.
🌈 Seven colors — the hues revealed when sunlight is dispersed.
🌍 Seven worlds — His light reaches across the entire expanse of creation described in our tradition.
🎶 Seven notes (Swaras) — the sound and rhythm of creation.
🪷 Seven chakras — symbols of the journey of consciousness within us.
One Sun,
but the light, time, rhythm, and life force linked to Him take countless forms.
Om Suryaya Namaha ॥
